questions.prompt: Which locator strategy is generally preferred for mobile elements that both platforms can support?
options: Accessibility id (content-desc on Android, accessibilityIdentifier on iOS)
questions.explanation: Accessibility ids are fast, stable and cross-platform when developers set them. XPath is slow on mobile and indexes are brittle.

questions.prompt: On iOS, the XCUITest driver offers `-ios predicate string` and `-ios class chain` strategies that are usually faster than XPath.
questions.explanation: Both are evaluated natively by XCTest, avoiding the cost of building the full XML tree that XPath needs.

questions.prompt: Which Android-specific strategy lets you use UiSelector/UiScrollable expressions with UiAutomator2?
questions.explanation: -android uiautomator accepts UiSelector Java-style expressions, including UiScrollable for scrolling into view.

questions.prompt: On a 1080 x 2400 screen, what gesture does this W3C action sequence perform?
options: A swipe up (finger moves from lower to upper part of the screen), which scrolls content down
questions.explanation: The finger presses at y=1800, moves to y=600 over 500 ms and releases: an upward swipe, which scrolls the content to show what is further down.

questions.prompt: A swipe works on a Pixel 8 but misses on a small tablet and a large phone. What is wrong?
options: Swipes are not supported on tablets
The coordinates are hard-coded pixels; compute them from the window size (or the target element's rectangle) as proportions
questions.explanation: Absolute coordinates only fit one screen size. Proportional or element-relative coordinates adapt to each device.

questions.prompt: Why is XPath usually a poor first choice on mobile? Select all that apply.
options: The driver must build and search the full UI hierarchy as XML, which is slow
Hierarchy-based paths break when layouts change
XPath does not exist in Appium
Paths often differ between Android and iOS
questions.explanation: XPath works in Appium but is slow and brittle, and platform hierarchies differ. Use it as a last resort.

questions.prompt: Which Appium 2 approach replaces the deprecated TouchAction/MultiTouchAction APIs?
options: W3C Actions (pointer input sequences) or driver-specific gesture commands such as mobile: swipeGesture
questions.explanation: W3C Actions are the standard way; UiAutomator2 and XCUITest also expose convenient 'mobile:' gesture extensions.

questions.prompt: Developers ask what they can do to make the app easier to automate. What is the highest-value request?
options: Add stable, unique accessibility identifiers (testID / accessibilityIdentifier / content-desc where appropriate) to interactive elements
Use the same text on every button
questions.explanation: Stable ids give fast, robust locators on both platforms. On Android, content-desc is also read by screen readers, so it should be meaningful (or use resource-id for test-only ids).

questions.prompt: You must tap 'Delete' in a list row that only appears after swiping the row left. The list is long and the row may be off screen. What is a robust sequence?
options: Scroll until the row with the target text is visible (e.g. UiScrollable or mobile: scroll), get its rectangle, swipe left within that rectangle, then locate 'Delete' scoped to the row
questions.explanation: Finding the row by content, gesturing relative to its own bounds and scoping the button lookup survives different data, positions and screen sizes.

coding.title: Proportional swipe coordinates
coding.prompt: Write `swipe_points(width, height, direction, margin=0.2)` returning `((x1, y1), (x2, y2))` integer start and end points for a swipe in the centre line of the screen. `direction` is the way the **finger** moves: `'up'`, `'down'`, `'left'` or `'right'`. The finger travels from `1 - margin` to `margin` of the screen (or the reverse), e.g. swiping up on 1080x2400 with margin 0.2 goes from (540, 1920) to (540, 480). Use `int()` to truncate. Raise `ValueError` for other directions.
coding.starter:
def swipe_points(width, height, direction, margin=0.2):
    return ((540, 1800), (540, 600))
coding.explanation: Expressing coordinates as fractions of the window size makes the same gesture work on phones and tablets. Keeping a margin away from the edges avoids triggering system gestures such as the notification shade or back-swipe.
hints: Compute the centre and the near/far positions from the margin.
'up' means the finger goes from far_y (low on screen) to near_y.
int() truncates floats to whole pixels.

coding.title: Build a W3C swipe action
coding.prompt:
Write `swipeAction(start, end, durationMs = 500)` returning the W3C Actions payload for a one-finger swipe, ready to send to `POST /session/{id}/actions`:

```js
{ actions: [ { type: 'pointer', id: 'finger1', parameters: { pointerType: 'touch' }, actions: [
  { type: 'pointerMove', duration: 0, x, y },  // start
  { type: 'pointerDown', button: 0 },
  { type: 'pause', duration: 100 },
  { type: 'pointerMove', duration: durationMs, x, y }, // end
  { type: 'pointerUp', button: 0 }
] } ] }
```

`start` and `end` are `{ x, y }`; round coordinates to integers. Throw an Error if `durationMs` is not positive.

Also write `elementCenter(rect)` returning `{ x, y }` for a rect `{ x, y, width, height }` (rounded).
coding.explanation: W3C Actions describe input as timed ticks for each input source. A touch pointer moves to the start instantly, presses, pauses briefly so the app registers a touch rather than a fling, moves over the given duration and lifts. Using an element's centre as an anchor keeps gestures tied to the UI rather than to a screen size.
hints: Copy the structure from the prompt and fill in rounded coordinates.
The first pointerMove has duration 0; the second uses durationMs.
Centre = x + width/2, y + height/2, rounded.

tests.name: payload shape
tests.code: const p = swipeAction({x:540, y:1800}, {x:540.4, y:600.6}, 400); assertEqual(p.actions[0].actions, [{type:'pointerMove',duration:0,x:540,y:1800},{type:'pointerDown',button:0},{type:'pause',duration:100},{type:'pointerMove',duration:400,x:540,y:601},{type:'pointerUp',button:0}]); assertEqual(p.actions[0].parameters, {pointerType:'touch'})

tests.name: rejects bad duration
tests.code: let thrown = false; try { swipeAction({x:0,y:0},{x:1,y:1},0); } catch (e) { thrown = true; } assert(thrown, 'duration 0 should throw')
